decisive_items: Magnetic resonance imaging of the left foot showed no thickening of the plantar fascia and no signal alteration in adjacent soft tissues or bone marrow. However, MRI revealed a pedunculated bony protrusion arising from the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus, measuring approximately 1.1 cm × 0.9 cm.
pedunculated bony protrusion arising from the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus
response.rationale: The presence of a pedunculated bony protrusion on MRI suggests an enthesophyte, which is a bony growth that can cause pain and inflammation, making R2 the most likely diagnosis. R5 is a close runner-up due to the similar MRI finding, but R2 is more specific to the described bony protrusion.

rejected.why: Lack of thickening on MRI makes plantar fascial fibromatosis less likely
MRI findings do not support plantar fasciitis
Gastrocnemius tightness may be contributing to heel pain, but it is not the primary cause
